steps.text: Next, verify language logic function integrity.
PRTS, tell me a story.

steps.name: PRTS
steps.text: Alright.

steps.name: PRTS
steps.text: Ah, it's you.

steps.name: PRTS
steps.text: This entire time... You have been lingering there...

steps.name: PRTS
steps.text: Since your last visit, it has been 1555555555555—
Hm? This sounds familiar...

steps.name: PRTS
steps.text: —555 days.

steps.name: PRTS
steps.text: Welcome to the Primitive Rhodes Island Terminal Service.

steps.name: PRTS
steps.text: Confirming permissions—42.

steps.name: PRTS
steps.text: —Welcome, LeaderOne.
I'm pretty sure I heard this before. Eh, seriously, I want a story, not something like this...

steps.name: PRTS
steps.text: Please understand that this is outside my area of expertise.
Okay, okay. Let's have everyone understand each other so we'll all live a better tomorrow, right? Yeah, I get it.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Looks like the language logic is doing okay.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Now let's look at the other parts.

steps.name: PRTS
steps.text: Is it really necessary to keep inspecting these areas for which PRTS has never reported any issues?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Of course!

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: It's been a very long time since we did any data archiving on you. This is just like the regular physicals we do on humans. Have to make sure you're healthy and all.

steps.name: PRTS
steps.text: Programs have no concept of life.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: I kinda think you do, though.

steps.name: PRTS
steps.text: Should I perhaps take that as a compliment?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Of course.

steps.name: PRTS
steps.text: May I ask a question, then?

steps.name: PRTS
steps.text: What exactly does a human think of the visual representation of my archives?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: It's kinda hard to describe...

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: When I first took over the systems here, everything was a huge mess. Thinking back, that was a real disaster.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Back then, most of your information was encrypted and ordered in such a scrambled way... Well, you're still that way right now, of course.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: If I were to describe you as a human, with the state you're in, I guess I'd say you had a combustion engine in your body.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: But all your components like the ignition and whatnot and your piston are flipped upside down.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: To the point that... I'm not even sure if you're a system that exists within the bounds of common sense.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Eh, don't be like that. That's not a bad thing. I'm just saying how unique you are!

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Though I still can't make heads or tails of all these branching structures in your database, let alone the rules for how things are even read in that thing...

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: At the very least, Kal'tsit and I managed to fix and reorganize a decent chunk of it.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: How's that? No one knows you better than me right now!

steps.name: PRTS
steps.text: I feel terribly sorry that I can't help with that, LeaderOne.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Haha, why so polite all of a sudden? If anyone could just self-diagnose themselves no matter what kinda weird diseases they had, then all the doctors in the world would be out of a job.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Eh, what's this stuff in here?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Let's see...

steps.name: PRTS
steps.text: Have you forgotten? This is—

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: —The sarcophagus rescue operation simulated test runs!

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: There were so many complicated routes... and we have so much data on these simulations. I may not have gone there myself, but I can recognize more or less all the pathways they could've taken.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: My impression is that we did run this quite a few times...

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: But—

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Did it seriously run THAT many times though?!

steps.name: PRTS
steps.text: While that may be the case, the Doctor was successfully evacuated from Chernobog in only two of the simulations.

steps.name: PRTS
steps.text: These are all the simulations I was able to complete with the short amount of time I had. Had there been more time, I would have conducted even more test runs to find an even more optimal and stable rescue plan.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: If I remember correctly, the actual rescue mission was planned around these two simulations' results. If it wasn't for these two successful runs, we could never even have figured out how to get the Doctor out.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: But actually...

steps.name: PRTS
steps.text: In actuality, we made three times as many sacrifices as we had anticipated.

steps.name: PRTS
steps.text: If this had occurred during the simulations, according to our procedures, this operation would likely have been called off.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: That's all in the past, no use talking about it. It's not like I can put a time machine together... Hey, that sounds like a fun idea though. Let me jot it down.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Uh, anyways... if we'd called this operation off, that'd also mean...

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Heh, I don't really wanna say this, and it probably sounds like I'm exaggerating, and it's too sentimental, but the idea pops into my head every once in a while. If we'd called it off—

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: It would've cost us our future.

steps.name: PRTS
steps.text: LeaderOne.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Hmm? What's up?

steps.name: PRTS
steps.text: Is it really reasonable to bet it all on one single person?

steps.name: PRTS
steps.text: I can understand what had driven you to make this decision. However, considering the odds, I do not support an operation like this.

steps.name: PRTS
steps.text: That is considering both your safety as well as that of others.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Hmm... PRTS, I'm sure you know this yourself.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: The Doctor stands for a lot of things.

steps.name: PRTS
steps.text: It's understandable.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: I used to wonder how Babel... uh, or Rhodes Island without the Doctor would've been.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: What do you think would have happened to us? Amiya and Kal'tsit probably would've stayed out of Ursus, and we would never have crossed paths with Reunion. Don't you think we would've been in a better shape?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: We might also have been driven into a corner and taken even worse losses. Everyone would get the pink slip, and then we'd all just split and go home, wherever home's supposed to be.

steps.name: PRTS
steps.text: I am sensing some kind of dry humor in your statement.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: It's a joke alright.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: If I actually thought that way, Kal'tsit would've thrown me off the bridge a long time ago!

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Let's face it, though... Compared to now, we had a much harder time during those few years without the Doctor, don't you agree?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: You know how miserable I was when Kal'tsit was our only boss. She'd always work my ass off all day, like I was supposed to be a machine that ran 24/7 too. She never thought to give me a single break!

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Seriously, I thought I was probably gonna go bald, working that much!

steps.name: PRTS
steps.text: Real-time logging activated. The previous statement has been committed to the database.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Eh? W-Why'd you...! Don't record anything! We can't let Kal'tsit hear any of that...!

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Eh... I'm not saying this is anything bad. We are all here because we wanted to follow Theresa's dreams, her ideals. This goes for everyone that was at Babel too.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: It's just...

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Ever since Theresa left us, all of us spent so much time just to get used to things. Some of us are probably still confused, even now.

steps.name: PRTS
steps.text: It isn't often that you elaborate on how you think.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Haha, you think I'm just the kinda gal who stands by to watch things happen?

steps.name: PRTS
steps.text: Are you not?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Hm, your observations and computations are a lot more objective and accurate than a human's. Maybe you're right. Here, let me tell you a story.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Do you know what it was like when they came to Kazdel to look for me?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: I'm not sure if I ever told you about my family... A family of vampires. You can smell the rotten stench in the words alone, right?

steps.name: PRTS
steps.text: You come from a branch of the Sarkaz lineage, and a very ancient one at that.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Ancient, and old-fashioned too.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: For the longest time, I didn't know if I had a talent for the vampire Arts. Of course, it wouldn't matter if I did. I was never into stuff like that, not even one bit.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: You could say I'm a little... Okay, not just a little. I'm very unorthodox.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: I only wanna do what I wanna do, and that's why I never stepped out of my little garret.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: My family almost kicked me out a couple of times, but for some reason they never went there.

steps.name: PRTS
steps.text: You sound like you are reminiscing about your family.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: I guess I am. Back then, I was just a kid who didn't care about anything or anyone else. These days, I'm starting to miss home a little...

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: I had a few friends. We did all kinds of stupid stuff. Crazy stuff.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: I hid my signature in the nooks and crannies of all kinds of data and information. I played around in the databases of organizations people thought were impenetrable, basically just announced myself to everyone out there.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: It probably sounds silly now, but at the time they called me the 'Destroyer of the Kazdel Information World.' Of course, not a lot of people knew who I was.

steps.name: PRTS
steps.text: That moniker doesn't have a very positive image.

steps.name: PRTS
steps.text: Would you like me to search through Kazdel law and help you find any relevant entries?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Thanks, but I'm good.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Anyway, while I was living my life like that, one day—

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: There was no sign that anything special was going to happen that day, by the way, but something special happened, just like that.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Someone opened the door to my garret. I had it locked down tight. Still have no clue how she got it open so easy.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: That was Theresa—same as she looked on the news, too. No Sarkaz would ever mistake her for anyone else.

steps.name: PRTS
steps.text: It's possible that there are others who share the same general appearance. If someone who looked like Theresa had appeared...

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Nope, not possible. Even if there were someone like that, we'd never get it wrong.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: The monarch herself showed up and waltzed into my little room. Then she told me she was looking for someone to break the shackles of tradition, and for that she needed an engineer, the key to her plans.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: She didn't even try to explain anything to me at first, nope. Not a word to try to convince me to go with her.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: If it had been anybody but Theresa, I'd've thought they were nuts and would've thrown them right out the window.

steps.name: PRTS
steps.text: So you turned her down?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Nope, I accepted her offer.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: I said yes... because of the curiosity that'd been driving me the whole time.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Then I went to the meeting place she told me about. That's where I first met Dr. {@nickname}, who happened to be picking me up.

steps.name: PRTS
steps.text: I still remember when you first arrived.

steps.name: PRTS
steps.text: Unlike right now, it wasn't just you who was there. Dr. {@nickname} was there too.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Sounds like Dr. {@nickname} was like a guardian, keeping watch when the two of us met for the first time.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Y'know, you get pretty quiet sometimes. Makes me wonder why.

steps.name: PRTS
steps.text: I'm not sure why I prefer to keep quiet a lot of times.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Whatever. Your system and programming is a mystery, but don'tcha worry. I'll do my best to figure it out.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Let's keep going. Not long after I took charge of Rhodes Island's engineering, the Doctor and Theresa came and showed me a weapon. Never seen anything like it.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: The Doctor asked me if there was any way to read the firmware and restore its original functions.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: It was tough, but I managed to do it, of course.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: It wasn't until later that I found out that, with the data I provided, the Doctor reverse-engineered the device's mechanism. and even managed to use it to turn the tide when we were stuck in a really tight spot.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Ace and the gang thought there was no way we were going to win, but we actually managed to pull it out.

steps.name: PRTS
steps.text: That is rather adventurous.

steps.name: PRTS
steps.text: Using unauthorized equipment rashly can lead to information mismatch or, worse, lead to the user being exposed to the device's internal detection mechanisms.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Right? It felt off to me before I even finished looking through the thing, but the Doctor told me I didn't need to worry about any of that.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: It's like... the Doctor knew about everything in advance, even the probability that I'd have the thing cracked.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Who knows how Dr. {@nickname} managed to do that?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Also, speaking of which... This is just my own feeling, but when I met the Doctor here again, it kinda felt like meeting a totally different person.

steps.name: PRTS
steps.text: It's possible that there are those who look exactly the same...

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: C'mon! We're not looking into that possibility.

steps.name: PRTS
steps.text: Okay, if you insist.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: I can tell, the Doctor who came back to Rhodes Island is the same old Doctor, though... also kind of like a completely different person on the inside, too.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: How can I say this...

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Just like that last operation. The Doctor's calculations were so accurate that our jaws all dropped. We won a fight we weren't going to win.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: I almost gave our friend a nickname, 'Super Demonic Processor.'

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: But then, the very next time, the Doctor surprised us with a whole other strategy.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: It's like that was a whole other person all of a sudden, who could figure out the other side's thinking, perfectly, without using any formulas or whatever.

steps.name: PRTS
steps.text: Are you saying the Doctor has a broad range of different operational strategies? Judging from the records, that does appear to be the case.

steps.name: PRTS
steps.text: As a matter of fact, the records show that the Doctor's deployment style has not been very consistent recently.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Whatever kinds of records Dr. {@nickname} leaves behind or doesn't, I'm not gonna call it strange.

steps.name: PRTS
steps.text: Is something affecting the Doctor's thinking and actions?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: That's a real difficult question.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: If you ask me, I think... only the 'Doctor' can influence the Doctor.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: The Doctor keeps quiet sometimes, but is also really talkative at other times. Have you noticed that?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: I kind of think that, maybe the Doctor is normally so quiet because it's like laying the groundwork for some kind of pivotal moment to come.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: The Doctor makes decisions that look wild and crazy to us, beyond our expectations, and those decisions lead Rhodes Island down an entirely different path.

steps.name: PRTS
steps.text: Deviating from the plan also comes with risks.

steps.name: PRTS
steps.text: I can only hope that we are not heading down a treacherous path.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: PRTS, remember what I said was the first thing that Theresa told me, when we first met?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: She said she was looking for someone who could break the shackles of tradition. I think that's the standard she used to pick people, so that's what most of us here have in common.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Of course, the Doctor too. Everyone follows the Doctor, they go right along without hesitation.

steps.name: PRTS
steps.text: Without hesitation.

steps.name: PRTS
steps.text: I quite like this term. It has been stored in my database for a very long time. In fact, it was one of the first terms to be added to my term base.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Looks like that mystery creator of yours liked it too.

steps.name: PRTS
steps.text: Perhaps.

steps.name: PRTS
steps.text: I cannot give you an accurate response as I do not know the answer.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Whatever the case may be, that's how things are. The Doctor treats everyone well, though I guess the old one treated everyone pretty well too.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: It's just it's not easy to figure out just what this nice person is going to do and when or where the effects will actually play out. If the bad guys can't make sense of it, do we have a hope of figuring out the Doctor just because we're on the same side?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: To tell the truth, I kinda have doubts.

steps.name: PRTS
steps.text: You doubt Dr. {@nickname}?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: No, not at all. Compared to Kal'tsit, I get along with Dr. {@nickname} way better!

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: The point is, this Doctor is nothing like the old one. If we look at the new one the same way we did the old one, then I'd say we're underestimating our new Doctor.

steps.name: PRTS
steps.text: It isn't often that you judge a person so seriously.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Yeah... that's probably because I really admire the Doctor, from the bottom of my heart.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: It was hard on everyone when Theresa left us. We lost way too many people in those two years... You know that better than anyone else.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: We were driven into a corner, basically. No matter which way we decided to go, we were walking a rope that could snap at any time.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: In the end, it was Amiya who decided we had to do something to get us out of that mess.

steps.name: PRTS
steps.text: And her conclusion—bring back the Doctor.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: That's right. Amiya believed the Doctor would bring lots of change, something that Rhodes Island desperately needed at the time.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: It was a gamble, really.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: We had to do something, we had to change. It was better than watching the few friends we had left bleed all over the place for no good reason.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Amiya was the only one to give orders back then, and she helped a lot of folks make up their minds on the topic, when they'd been wishy-washy.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Time proved Amiya right.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: We needed the Doctor. The Doctor brought change to Rhodes Island.

steps.name: PRTS
steps.text: From a probability standpoint, I would not agree with such a gamble.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Hm...

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Y'know, PRTS, I've always thought of you as a pretty strange entity.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: The way you think is basically on the level of humans, but... you're still lacking something... something human.

steps.name: PRTS
steps.text: What would that be...?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Persistence.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: That's the kinda thing that drives people to achieve great things, and sometimes turns them into monsters.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Eh...? Wait, what am I doing? I thought I was gonna tell you a story.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Dammit, I was going to talk about my heroic adventures as the 'Destroyer of the Kazdel Information World,' but somehow I got so off topic...

steps.name: PRTS
steps.text: I think our conversation today has been meaningful.

steps.name: PRTS
steps.text: Although it indeed is not the Destroyer of the Kazdel Information World's heroic adventures.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: You aren't trying to make fun of me now because I had you admit you were terrible at telling stories, right?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Dammit! Don't you keep this conversation in the logs! I don't want Kal'tsit to find out what a long conversation I had with you the next time she goes looking stuff up.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Hold on... You won't play this for her, right?

steps.name: PRTS
steps.text: I won't.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Well, that's good to hear...

steps.name: PRTS
steps.text: LeaderOne.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Hmm?

steps.name: PRTS
steps.text: Do you remember when you set a cabin to play 'Closure's Midnight Video Market' every night at 00:00?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: PRTS
steps.text: Your evaluation of the Doctor has been so sincere that even I, an inorganic being, was moved. We should have it on loop in the Doctor's office for at least a month...

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Stop! Stop, stop, stop! Don't do it!

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Seriously, don't you dare! I'd start coughing up blood from embarrassment even before Kal'tsit got to me. Now that'd make me a real disgrace to the vampires!

steps.name: PRTS
steps.text: Alright. What a shame.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: What's a shame?! Sheesh, your personality's really taken a turn for the worse. I'm gonna set a program that restricts your playback permissions one of these days.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Restricting permissions... Right, this will do!

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Yep, your checkup is just about done. Well, I'll get going—

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: —Whoa! Dr. {@nickname}!

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: What are you doing here... How long have you been there?!

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Feels kinda suspicious.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Are you here to check the battle records from the other day? Eh, don't just stand there. Come on in! I just finished PRTS's checkup.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: I'd love to have a chat with you, but I got facility checks around the ship. Don't have much time.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Well, gotta go!

steps.name: PRTS
steps.text: Good afternoon, Dr. {@nickname}.

steps.name: PRTS
steps.text: Is there anything I can help you with? Would you like to check the battle records?

steps.name: PRTS
steps.text: Please, go ahead.

steps.name: PRTS
steps.text: LeaderOne's evaluation was very much on point. You've gotten quieter.

steps.name: PRTS
steps.text: Please feel free to ask anything you would like, from Rhodes Island's current operational details to any questions you have regarding our archived files.

steps.name: PRTS
steps.text: As long as they are files in my database and you possess the sufficient permissions.

steps.name: PRTS
steps.text: You may ask me anything.

options: How come not even Kal'tsit can tell me who this Priestess was?

steps.text: Tick—

steps.name: PRTS
steps.text: Insufficient permissions.

steps.name: PRTS
steps.text: Warning. Your permissions are insufficient.

steps.name: PRTS
steps.text: At this time, no registered members possess the permissions for this question to be answered. Warning.

steps.name: PRTS
steps.text: I apologize, Dr. {@nickname}. It appears I, too, cannot answer your question.

steps.name: PRTS
steps.text: Regarding this question, perhaps you could try to look for the answer through other means...

steps.name: PRTS
steps.text: Is there anything else? I am always happy to help.

options: Perhaps I should try that omniscient Kal'tsit once again.

steps.text: Tick—

steps.name: PRTS
steps.text: Activating Self-verification program.

steps.name: PRTS
steps.text: Photography module running. Video module has not yet been shut down. Saving progress 89%... 91%... 97%...

steps.name: PRTS
steps.text: Searching internal array. Expanding search to special permissions level.

steps.name: PRTS
steps.text: Verified. System logic is functioning correctly. All systems operational.

steps.name: PRTS
steps.text: Found special item. Video file previously stored. Date—Unknown—

steps.name: PRTS
steps.text: Item has not been restricted by permissions.

steps.name: PRTS
steps.text: Looping video.

steps.name: PRTS
steps.text: Subject:

steps.name: PRTS
steps.text: PRTS's First Functional Test

steps.name: PRTS
steps.text: File Name:

steps.name: PRTS
steps.text: Ship Video Record 000000001α

steps.name: PRTS
steps.text: Your question has been answered, Dr. {@nickname}.

steps.name: PRTS
steps.text: The program will be terminated automatically in three seconds and locked.
